{"summary":"Research memo — complete `msw` inventory for a macOS status-bar monitor. Evidence: authoritative dispatch is `bin/msw:1809-1888`; command behavior is implemented at `bin/msw:474-1753`; user documentation is `docs/MSW-CHEATSHEET.md:3-218`, `docs/SETUP-GUIDE.md:72-323`, and `docs/GITHUB-SETUP.md:84-247`. Fixed workspaces are `dev`, `playgrounds`, and `personal` (`bin/msw:12,43-59`); paths are restricted beneath `/workspace` (`bin/msw:399-419`). Classification below uses RO=pure read-only, RO*=logically read-only but starts a stopped VM, M=mutating, D=destructive, and E=temporary mutation restored afterward.

Global dependencies/output: every invocation first requires and sources `MSW_CONFIG_FILE`, defaulting to `~/.config/msw/config.sh` (`bin/msw:4-10`). Only help, version, and docs bypass the subsequent `msb` executable check (`bin/msw:1813-1817`); even `url`, `ports`, and `github status` therefore require installed `msb` when invoked through the wrapper. Configuration supplies names/IPs, resource defaults and ceilings, published ports, GitHub secret hosts, backup directory, and docs directory (`config.sh:5-55`). The installed CLI was verified as `msb 0.6.8`. The wrapper has no global JSON mode and emits human text/ANSI, so the monitor should use argument arrays, exit status, and direct read-only `msb` JSON telemetry while retaining `msw` for lifecycle mutations because `msw start/restart` injects the host-held guest token safely (`bin/msw:331-378,545-560`).

Inventory:
• `msw dev|playgrounds|personal [PATH]` and generic `msw shell WORKSPACE [PATH]`: M (may start VM; interactive shell can mutate anything), expose only as “Open Terminal” quick actions. PATH defaults to `/workspace`; otherwise it must be relative. Output is an interactive SSH/zsh session, not parseable. Dependencies: msb, configured sandbox, SSH alias/proxy/key; evidence `bin/msw:474-482,1819-1825` and cheatsheet `:5-12`.
• `msw zed WORKSPACE [PATH]`: M (auto-start plus external-app launch), expose as a project quick action. Default `/workspace`; output is only process status. Dependencies: msb, SSH integration, installed executable Zed CLI; `bin/msw:484-492,1827-1829`.
• `msw exec WORKSPACE COMMAND...`: M/arbitrary and unsafe as a generic UI facility; do not expose except internally with a fixed allowlist. It auto-starts and runs from `/workspace`; stdout/stderr and exit code belong to the supplied command, so there is no stable schema. Dependencies: msb and guest command; `bin/msw:381-396,582-587,1869`.
• `msw clone WORKSPACE OWNER/REPO [PATH]`: M; omit from the primary monitor or place in an advanced repository workflow with validated fields and explicit destination review. PATH defaults to repository name; creates parents and refuses an existing destination. Git progress is human output; rely on exit status then refresh `repos`. Dependencies: running/auto-started VM, guest Git, network, and guest read credential for private repositories; `bin/msw:744-747,785-810,1844-1847`.
• `msw repos WORKSPACE`: RO*; reasonable on-demand project submenu, never background-poll because it starts the VM. Output is a sorted newline-delimited list of workspace-relative repository paths; usable cautiously as line records but not formal JSON. Dependencies: msb, VM, guest `find/sed/sort`; `bin/msw:812-823,1848`.
• `msw pull WORKSPACE [PATH|all]`: M; do not expose as a casual menu click. Default is `all`; each repository runs `git pull --ff-only --prune`, continuing across all and failing overall if any cannot fast-forward. Output is human Git text. Dependencies: auto-started VM, guest Git/network/read token; `bin/msw:825-841,1849-1852`.
• `msw push WORKSPACE PATH [--yes|-y] [--force-with-lease]`: M and remote-destructive when rewriting history; normally keep outside the status app. If exposed, require a full review sheet showing repository, path, branch, exact commit, fast-forward mode, and commits, preserve typed `PUSH`, never pass `--yes`, and add a second warning for force-with-lease. Default is fast-forward-only; force uses an exact observed remote SHA. Human summary only, followed by success text; no machine schema. Dependencies: auto-started VM, guest and host Git, macOS Keychain write token, askpass helper, msb copy, network, and optionally git-lfs/shasum; `bin/msw:984-1099` and security boundary `docs/GITHUB-SETUP.md:192-238`.
• `msw identity "NAME" EMAIL [WORKSPACE|all]`: M; settings-only, not monitor UI. Target defaults to all and writes guest global Git configuration. Output is one fixed-width human row per workspace. Dependencies: auto-started VM and guest Git; `bin/msw:775-783,1858-1861`.
• `msw github` with no subcommand and `msw github status [WORKSPACE|all]`: RO; expose optionally as credential-health badges. Target defaults to all. Output is a fixed-width table containing only guest-read presence, host-write presence, and verification repository—never token values; parse conservatively or add a future JSON adapter. Dependencies: msb gate, macOS Keychain/security, metadata files; `bin/msw:1311-1320,1343-1356` and `docs/GITHUB-SETUP.md:128-134`.
• `msw github setup WORKSPACE OWNER/REPO [--read-only]`: M and security-sensitive; do not expose in the menu bar, or use a dedicated settings wizard with hidden inputs and no captured logs. Default mode requires separate guest-read and host-write tokens; `--read-only` removes host write access. It writes Keychain/metadata, changes the VM secret binding, quarantines during the transaction, and runs verification with rollback on failure. Human interactive output only. Dependencies: msb, Keychain/security, lockf, Git/GitHub/network, askpass, existing sandbox; `bin/msw:1194-1309,1346-1349` and `docs/GITHUB-SETUP.md:84-126`.
• `msw github verify WORKSPACE [OWNER/REPO]`: E/M remotely; settings-only with a strong warning because host-write mode creates and deletes a temporary remote branch. Repository and access mode default from metadata. It restarts/rebinds the guest secret, clones a temporary checkout, verifies guest push rejection, optionally verifies host push, and cleans up. Human pass/fail output and exit status only. Same GitHub dependencies as setup; `bin/msw:1114-1192,1350-1353`.
• `msw github remove WORKSPACE`: D for credentials and access; settings-only with explicit confirmation naming the workspace. It deletes metadata and both Keychain items, removes the guest secret with restart, and quarantines on incomplete cleanup. Human success/error output only. Dependencies: msb, Keychain/security, lockf, existing sandbox where present; `bin/msw:1322-1341,1357-1360`.
• `msw url WORKSPACE [PORT] [http|https]`: RO and ideal as an internal URL builder/copy action. Defaults are port 3000 and HTTP; port must be 1–65535 and prepublished. Output is exactly one URL line. Dependencies: config plus the wrapper’s msb gate; `bin/msw:467-500,1835-1838`.
• `msw open WORKSPACE [PORT] [http|https]`: M (auto-start) and core quick action. Same defaults/validation as `url`; display the URL before opening and disable unavailable ports. Human note plus macOS browser launch, so use exit status rather than parsing. Dependencies: msb, sandbox, `/usr/bin/open`, configured hostname; `bin/msw:503-509,1831-1834`.
• `msw ports [WORKSPACE|all]`: RO; expose as informational/settings data. Target defaults to all. Output is a descriptive human block, not machine-readable; the app should read the installed config or derive ports from direct `msb status` JSON instead. Published ports and reserved health-check ports are documented at `config.sh:46-48` and cheatsheet `:107-117`; implementation `bin/msw:447-465,511-526,1839`.
• `msw tunnel WORKSPACE REMOTE_PORT [LOCAL_PORT]`: M (auto-start plus persistent SSH process); advanced action only, with an active-tunnel row and explicit Stop control. LOCAL defaults to REMOTE; both must be 1–65535. Output is a human mapping and the process remains attached until cancellation. Dependencies: msb, SSH integration, free local port; `bin/msw:625-633,1840-1843`.
• `msw start [WORKSPACE|all]`: M and core. Target defaults to all; prefer explicit per-workspace actions, confirm “all,” serialize operations, and show progress. Human notes plus `<workspace>: running`; refresh state from JSON afterward. Dependencies: msb, sandbox and Keychain read token when configured; `bin/msw:333-378,528-531,1863`.
• `msw stop [WORKSPACE|all]`: M with workload/data-loss risk after graceful timeout; core but confirm per workspace and strongly confirm all. Target defaults to all; wrapper requests a 60-second graceful stop. Output is a stopping note or `<workspace>: already stopped`. Dependencies: msb; `bin/msw:533-543,1864`. Installed `msb stop` help confirms timeout expiry can force-kill, risking un-fsynced writes.
• `msw restart [WORKSPACE|all]`: M with interruption risk; core/advanced with confirmation and progress. Target defaults to all and uses a 60-second timeout while preserving guest-token injection. Human note only. Dependencies: msb, sandbox, Keychain read token when configured; `bin/msw:545-560,1865`.
• `msw status` and undocumented alias `msw ps`: RO and the primary polling function conceptually, but do not parse wrapper output. The wrapper prints `msb ps -a --label msw.managed=true` followed by human port documentation (`bin/msw:563-567,1866`). Use direct `msb status -a --label msw.managed=true --format json`; verified installed output is a JSON array with name, status, CPU, memory/max-memory, image, command, and port mappings.
• `msw metrics [WORKSPACE|all]`: RO continuous and core telemetry, but wrapper always execs `msb metrics --watch`, producing an in-place TTY table (`bin/msw:569-574,1867`). For the app use direct one-shot `msb metrics --all --format json` or long-lived `msb metrics --follow --interval 1s` JSON Lines, cancel on app shutdown, and join by workspace name. Installed JSON was verified to include CPU, memory/limit/host-resident, disk and network counters, upper-disk usage/free, uptime, state, timestamp, and vCPU time. It does not auto-start stopped VMs.
• `msw logs WORKSPACE [MSB LOG OPTIONS]`: RO and useful as an on-demand advanced panel. It does not auto-start. Prefer `msw logs WORKSPACE --json --tail N`, optionally `--follow`; installed help also supports since/until, timestamps, source, grep, session IDs, and color controls. JSON mode emits JSON Lines. Dependencies: msb and retained sandbox logs; `bin/msw:576-580,1868`.
• `msw disk [WORKSPACE|all]`: RO* and useful only on demand because it starts stopped VMs. Target defaults to all; output combines colored workspace headings, `df -h`, and `docker system df`, with no stable schema. Parse neither; use fixed internal guest commands with explicit machine formats if a disk widget is required. Dependencies: msb, guest bash/df/Docker; `bin/msw:589-596,1870`.
• `msw resize WORKSPACE MEMORY [CPUS]`: M; advanced settings only with current/maximum values, validation, and confirmation. MEMORY is required, CPUS optional. The wrapper merely calls `msb modify` and does not itself enforce `MSW_*_MAX_MEMORY/MAX_CPUS`, despite the docs saying “within configured limits”; the app must validate against `config.sh:22-36`. Wrapper output is underlying human msb output; direct `msb modify` supports JSON, dry-run, next-start, and restart, but those are not surfaced by `msw`. Evidence `bin/msw:598-603,1871`.
• `msw clean [WORKSPACE|all] [--volumes]`: D; hide from the main monitor and place behind a maintenance confirmation. Target defaults to all. Without the flag it irreversibly prunes unused containers, images, networks, and build cache; `--volumes` additionally deletes unused volumes and needs a stronger typed warning. Docker human progress only. Dependencies: auto-started VM and Docker; `bin/msw:843-865,1872`, warning in setup guide `:315-319`.
• `msw upgrade [WORKSPACE|all]`: M and potentially disruptive; maintenance-only with explicit target confirmation, progress/log window, and no concurrent lifecycle action. Default all; runs apt update, full-upgrade, autoremove, and clean. Human apt output only. Dependencies: auto-started VM, guest apt/network; `bin/msw:605-611,1873`.
• `msw update`: M of host tooling; settings/maintenance only with confirmation and restart expectations. It uses Homebrew when the tapped package is installed, otherwise `msb self update`, then runs doctor. Human output only. Dependencies: msb and optionally Homebrew/network; `bin/msw:613-623,1874`.
• `msw check` and `msw check --deep`: quick mode is RO diagnostic; deep mode is E/M. Expose quick “Run health check” on demand using exit status and captured human output. Deep must be explicitly labeled disruptive: it starts stopped VMs, checks guest/system/Docker/internet/SSH, starts temporary HTTP and nginx services on reserved ports 24678/24679, cleans them up, and attempts to restore originally stopped state. Dependencies: msb/doctor and host integration; deep additionally SSH, curl, guest systemd/Python/Docker/network. Evidence `bin/msw:1380-1468,1875`.
• `msw host repair`: M, privileged and host-wide; hide under troubleshooting and launch in Terminal because it requires sudo. It rewrites managed `/etc/hosts` content, loopback LaunchDaemon, SSH keys/config, and authorization. Human output only. Dependencies: macOS, sudo, launchctl/network utilities, ssh-keygen, msb; `bin/msw:655-742,1876-1879`.
• `msw backup [DIRECTORY]`: M to lifecycle and filesystem but recovery-oriented; expose as an advanced maintenance action with destination chooser, sensitive-archive warning, progress, cancellation handling, and mutation lock. Destination defaults to `MSW_BACKUP_DIR` (`~/Backups/microsandbox` in packaged config). It records running VMs, syncs/stops them, creates sparse zstd archive/checksum/info files, then restarts only prior-running VMs. No JSON; after human progress it prints archive, checksum, and info paths on three lines, but a future JSON adapter is safer than positional parsing. Dependencies: msb, gtar, zstd, shasum, writable storage; `bin/msw:1470-1572,1886` and setup guide `:266-288`.
• `msw restore ARCHIVE [--yes|-y]`: D; do not expose in the normal monitor. A recovery wizard must verify the archive/sidecar, display rollback location, retain typed `RESTORE`, never pass `--yes`, stop all activity, and instruct post-restore repair/check. It validates members, stages transactionally, replaces all managed state, rolls back on failure, and leaves VMs stopped. Human output only. Dependencies: msb, gtar, zstd, shasum, sufficient storage; `bin/msw:1574-1739,1887` and setup guide `:290-304`.
• `msw docs [TOPIC]`: RO; expose as Help links. Default `cheatsheet`; accepted aliases are `cheatsheet|commands`, `setup`, `github`, and `tests|test-report`. Output is installed Markdown through `$PAGER` on a TTY or `cat`; dependencies are config and files in `MSW_DOCS_DIR`, not msb. Evidence `bin/msw:1741-1753,1815`.
• `msw version|--version|-V`: RO; expose in About. Exact output is `msw <version>`; verified repository version is `msw 3.1.0`. Dependency: sourced config only; `config.sh:5`, `bin/msw:1813`.
• `msw help|--help|-h` and no-argument invocation: RO; expose in Help/About. Plain human command reference, no schema. Dependency: sourced config only; `bin/msw:1755-1814`.

Recommended monitor boundary: continuously read only direct msb status JSON and metrics JSON/JSONL; use `msw` for start/stop/restart so credential substitution and quarantine checks remain intact; offer logs, open URL, Terminal/Zed, disk, repos, ports, GitHub presence, quick check, and backup only on demand. Keep arbitrary exec, Git mutations, credential setup/removal, clean, upgrade, restore, and host repair out of the primary menu. Treat stdout as untrusted human text unless an explicit JSON/JSONL mode is documented, redact environment and Keychain data, serialize per-workspace mutations, and refresh authoritative JSON state after every action.

Verification was read-only: inspected all requested files, enumerated dispatch/functions, ran repository help/version, and inspected installed msb help plus read-only status/metrics JSON. No tests, formatters, linters, or mutating commands were run. No task files changed. Initial and final worktrees retained the same pre-existing `.gitignore`, `.smithers/`, `AGENTS.md`, and `smithers.db*` entries.","filesChanged":[]}
